name: 65DMA vs 50DMA
kill_criterion_result: 65DMA IC_IR >= 50DMA IC_IR in 5/6 construct x horizon comparisons (all dist/slope pairs both horizons, and 1Y stack; only 1M stack has 50DMA marginally ahead: 0.145 vs 0.135)
answer_to_principal: 65DMA wins (or ties) on IC_IR vs 50DMA in every comparison except one (1M stack score, a near-tie: 0.145 vs 0.135). The margin grows at the 1Y horizon (dist 0.686 vs 0.606, slope 0.717 vs 0.669, stack 0.947 vs 0.912) -- directionally consistent with the '50DMA is crowded/gamed, 65DMA is not' thesis. At 1M, DISTANCE-from-either-MA is actually NEGATIVE IC_IR for both lengths and fails the lag test badly (delta 1.4-1.8, mean-reversion artifact, not a clean trend signal) -- so the win for 65 at 1M is 'less bad', not tradeable. SLOPE is the construct that is both directionally right (+) and lag-stable at 1M for both lengths, and 65DMA-slope beats 50DMA-slope there too (0.126 vs 0.093).
harness_verdict: KILL (all 12 sub-cards) -- every H001 variant fails PBO>0.5 (CSCV), most 1M variants also fail the IC_IR>=0.20 floor and/or lag_test_delta<=0.25. DSR is also ~0 across the board (see ISSUE note).
note: [DATA] computed from rnd/panel/cube_close.parquet (751-symbol cube) via rnd/lib/builders_ma.py; dist=close/MA_n-1, slope=MA_n(t)/MA_n(t-21)-1, stack=count(close>MA_fast, MA_fast>MA150, MA150>MA200); basis=resid, run via rnd/run_ma_hypotheses.py. See ISSUE note in H002 card re: PBO/DSR near-universal fail.
